title: Non-Equilibrium Model Selection via Finite-Time Thermodynamics
abstract: Information criteria such as WAIC and WBIC extend model selection to singular learning machines, but they are usually derived for equilibrium posteriors. We formulate a finite-time analogue of WBIC by replacing the equilibrium posterior with an effective ensemble generated by learning dynamics under a resource constraint. When this ensemble admits an analytic effective potential, singular learning theory yields a resource-dependent real log canonical threshold. The resulting estimator gives a computable thermodynamic contribution to time-bounded MDL and identifies the finite-time singular complexity relevant to the structural information measured by epiplexity.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to adapt model selection techniques for complex statistical models operating under finite resources. It replaces equilibrium free energy calculations with a finite-time analogue by incorporating the dynamics of learning processes into singularity theory. This provides a new, resource-aware measure of model complexity relevant for time-bounded inference.
main_problem: The paper extends model selection criteria, traditionally derived from equilibrium statistical mechanics (like WAIC/WBIC), to the regime of finite-time, resource-constrained learning dynamics.
main_result: It formulates a finite-time analogue of Watanabe's BIC ($WBIC_R$), which replaces equilibrium complexity measures with a resource-dependent real log canonical threshold ($\lambda_R$).
method: The authors adapt singular learning theory by modeling the learning process as a stochastic path governed by a transition kernel, allowing for the calculation of an effective free energy based on this finite-time ensemble.
model_or_system: The model is statistical inference applied to machine learning, specifically addressing parameter estimation in singular models (like deep neural networks). The dynamics are approximated using processes like Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics (SGLD) under a resource constraint $R$.
key_observables: Finite-time free energy ($WBIC_R$), Resource-dependent Real Log Canonical Threshold ($\lambda_R$), and the structural information measure called epiplexity.
important_parameters: Resource constraint ($R$), Time horizon ($T$), Inverse temperature $ eta^* = 1/\ln N$, and the effective loss function $L_R(	heta)$.
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes that the endpoint density of the learning process can be locally represented by an analytic effective potential, which is crucial for applying singular theory.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the failure of classical criteria in singular models. It then develops the non-equilibrium extension by replacing equilibrium posteriors with ensembles generated by learning dynamics under resource constraints. The core mathematical machinery involves adapting singularity theory to this finite-time, path-dependent setting.
why_interesting: While focused on ML inference, the methodology of deriving complexity measures from dynamical processes and resource limitations has parallels in non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics, particularly when analyzing relaxation or measurement protocols that are inherently time-limited.
